subject.title: perf(sqlite): fast schema gates, background integrity verification, and downgrade protection

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed default fail-closed updater/startup behavior and daily database quarantine workflow for existing installations when schema inspection or verification cannot complete normally?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the product contract from retrying or proceeding to refusing updates/startup and potentially quarantining a live database; code review alone cannot choose the acceptable operator and availability tradeoff.

options.title: Require upgrade and recovery proof
options.body: Keep the proposed direction, but require maintainer-visible proof for schema-3 upgrades, pre-stop update refusal, lock/inspection failures, and Doctor recovery before merge.

options.title: Narrow the initial scope
options.body: Land only the cheap schema-version gate and updater preflight, deferring background quarantine and its new persistent state until its recovery policy is separately agreed.

recommendation.title: Require upgrade and recovery proof
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed direction, but require maintainer-visible proof for schema-3 upgrades, pre-stop update refusal, lock/inspection failures, and Doctor recovery before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the adjacent integrity and startup contracts that this PR changes in timing and scope.
